proved_negative_scope: Universal bare instantaneous Sobolev Gronwall bounds (order exponent r <= 0 with reservoir L2) fail on bounded R-585 solution families even at matching initial energy and charge, and the isolated coefficient-time form of one specified order-minus-two correction is not uniformly L2-form bounded. Neither obstruction is same-data nonuniqueness.
scope: Original R-585 common preparation and EXCH Hamiltonian, side-16 periodic T^3, exact K/2K carriers and original canonical time. Fixed finite windows, no added regularity, no new dynamics or regulator. The test compares different admissible initial preparations only to falsify a uniform method, not as a same-initial-value comparison.
order_difference_test: Let J=-i for the Hamiltonian law, and let cJJ, cJK, cKK here denote the effective pinned coefficients a,b,c in the R-585 note. On the first-component plane m1=m2=0, m3=rho. Thus original F_II=1/2 integral C(rho)|grad rho|^2 on that restriction, where C(rho)=a+2b d_rho/(rho+d_rho)+c[d_rho/(rho+d_rho)]^2. The two other generators vanish for the test variation, not necessarily for the subsequent flow.

Fix A>0 and let t_n=n^-3, A_n=A(1-t_n^2)/(1+t_n^2), q_n=2A t_n/(1+t_n^2), g_n=q_n cos(2 pi n x1/16). The two order initial values U_+=A_n+(1-i)g_n and U_-=A_n-(1-i)g_n are inserted in the first component and both reservoirs start at zero. Each is a common initial preparation for the original projections. They tend strongly in H2 to A e1. Averaged order norm squared equals A_n^2+q_n^2=A^2 for each sign; translation by half a wavelength swaps the two, so the full original Hamiltonian values agree at time zero.

Set w=U_+-U_-=2(1-i)g_n and kappa_n=2 pi n/16. At time zero half the bare L2 difference slope is the difference of real variations in direction i w. The complex-linear self-adjoint Fourier part cancels, local potentials contribute O(||w||_2^2), and the reservoir difference and both exchange contributions vanish at t=0. The Class-II test has delta rho_+=delta rho_-=4 A_n g_n and grad rho_+=(2 A_n+4g_n)grad g_n, grad rho_-=(-2 A_n+4g_n)grad g_n. The density difference in the Class-II variation has coefficient of |grad g_n|^2 equal to 16 A_n^2 C(A_n^2) at g_n=0 and converges uniformly to beta*4, beta=4 A^2 C(A^2)>0. Exact floor derivatives are included by the quotient rule. Since ||w||_2^2=8 integral g_n^2 and integral |grad g_n|^2=kappa_n^2 integral g_n^2, the slope-to-energy quotient is (beta+o(1))*kappa_n^2+O(1). For any fixed r<=0, the Sobolev weight (1+kappa_n^2)^r cancels in this quotient; the reservoir term in the norm is initially zero.

This slope computation applies to the actual R-585 weak solutions (each with its own smooth starting datum), not just finite ODEs. Truncate the difference with a fixed spatial Fourier projection in the quadratic energy identity and integrate in time. The fourth-order complex-linear skew part cancels exactly in every truncation. The remaining order force is C_t H^{-1}; the difference is C_t H^{15/8}, so the pairings with its projected Sobolev-weighted test converge uniformly for r<=0. The reservoir difference energy is differentiable by the L2 equation from the pointwise bound below. This gives the asserted initial derivative for every such weak branch.
positive_reservoir_reduction: The R-585 reservoir cubic is C_t L^{4/3}. Fubini in its time-integral equation yields an a.e. spatial pointwise absolutely continuous representative. Radial self terms are pure rotations, so |chi(t,x)| <= |chi0(x)| + epsilon integral |S(Psi)(s,x)| ds (integrate between 0 and t in either direction). Uniform H2 order and common bounded reservoir data give a derived L-infinity bound on each finite window. On this ball the reservoir difference is L2-Lipschitz in itself and in the forced order difference: ||dchi(t)||_2 <= C_T(||dchi(0)||_2+ integral ||dPsi||_2). This is not a pointwise bound on the Galerkin reservoirs.
modified_energy_attempt: The second-order first-component radial/phase matrix at A e1 is B=diag(beta,0); J does not commute with B. In the frozen principal two-dimensional system, the positive metric I+B/(Y*kappa^2) symmetrizes J(Y*kappa^4 I+kappa^2 B). Thus the bare slope does not even imply a frozen instability.

For a genuine variable background consider one natural symmetric correction C_z=Lambda^{-1} B_-(z) Lambda^{-1}/Y, with Lambda=(1-Delta)^{1/2} and B_-=(B+JBJ)/2, defined as a candidate form only. The separately estimated coefficient-time term D C_z[J grad H(z,0)] is not uniformly bounded on L2 from the H2 bound. On the first-component plane DB_-(A e1)[J e1]=[J,B_-(A e1)]/A by phase covariance (also by direct differentiation of 4 C(|z|^2) z z^T), so its pairing with v=(e1+i e1)/sqrt(2) is -beta/A.

For that isolated form take a real smooth nonzero bump phi compactly supported inside a coordinate cube, eta=phi^2, z_N=(A+N^-1/2 eta(N(x-x0)))e1 and y_N=Lambda^{-1}w_N=N^1/2 phi(N(x-x0))v. The backgrounds are H2-bounded and ||w_N||_2^2=||y_N||_{H1}^2 is bounded above and below. At these smooth states the original instantaneous order vector field has leading part Y J e1 N^{7/2}(Delta^2 eta)(N(x-x0)), with the lower terms O(N^{3/2}) on the supporting cube. The normalized isolated form is a nonzero constant times N^{3/2} integral phi^2 Delta^2 eta + O(N), using coefficient smoothness and z_N-A=O(N^-1/2). The integral is ||Delta(phi^2)||_2^2>0. Thus the separated time term cannot be bounded as C||w_N||_2^2 in absolute value. These are arbitrary tests for the proposed standalone bound, not a claimed actual difference of two solutions; cancellation with commutators or an integrated estimate is still possible.
independent_hostile_review: Separate exact checks by complex current quotient rule and by radial/phase realification, review of translation-matched H and Q, Fourier weight cancellation, weak energy testing, and independent localized coefficient-time obstruction. Onodera, arXiv:2411.00452v1, Theorem 1.1 (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.00452v1), is reference only: its 1D torus, H^m for m>=4 and structured nonlinearities do not supply an energy-class 3D EXCH uniqueness theorem.
missing_estimate: A combined, not termwise, bound for a positive difference energy equivalent to L2 at the stated regularity, controlling coefficient time and spatial commutator remainders together, or a genuine time-integrated substitute for this estimate. No such bound proved and no same-data counterexample.
reentry: Only on an explicit cancellation or spacetime estimate verified for the pinned 3D H2 Class-II difference, or a same-initial-data counterexample. Do not repeat the bare or separated-term Gronwall tests.
non_claims: No uniqueness or nonuniqueness result, no rejection of all modified energies, no refutation of R-585, no full-sequence convergence or energy equality, no C6/T-054 change, no physical Pre-A, QFT or gravity. No new Lean theorem or PDF required for this scoped route audit.
